classification.difficultyReason: Identify the sloping seam as the hypotenuse and use sine to calculate the vertical depth.

content.prompt:
An iron ore seam slopes down $120\text{ m}$ at an angle of depression from the horizontal of $38^\circ$.
The mine engineer wishes to sink a vertical shaft.
What is the depth of the required vertical shaft? Answer to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Unlabelled right triangle with a vertical left side, horizontal lower side and descending hypotenuse. A dashed horizontal reference extends right from the upper-left vertex; a right-angle square marks the lower-left vertex. Ordinary source blue and grey strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: The descending hypotenuse represents the 120 m ore seam. The upper horizontal reference establishes the angle of depression. The vertical left side represents the required shaft depth. Numerical givens occur only in the prompt, as in the source.
spec.answerVisibility: All source geometry is visible in the question; no teacher answer or added numerical labels.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the vertical depth. The angle between the seam and the lower horizontal is $38^\circ$, since the horizontal lines are parallel.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 38^\circ &= \frac{d}{120}\\d &= 120\sin 38^\circ\\d &\approx 74\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The required shaft is $74\text{ m}$ deep, to the nearest metre.
